package_info.package_versions: unknown (specific version not stated, but an old version in use)
package_info.why_malicious: The package was modified to include malicious JavaScript code at the end of a widely used library (modernizr), which was then used to skim payment form data and exfiltrate credit card details from users. This modification turned a legitimate library into a vehicle for a Magecart-style supply chain attack.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when payment form is loaded and used by the victim)
execution_context.file_location: modernizr.js (appended to the end of the legitimate library, served from BA's web server)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: This code attaches an event listener to the payment form. When the form is submitted, it collects credit card details (card number, expiration, CVV) and exfiltrates them to an external malicious server via an image request.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code surreptitiously collects sensitive payment data and sends it to an external domain, which is a classic sign of a skimmer or Magecart attack.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate JavaScript library like modernizr should not interact with payment forms or exfiltrate data. The presence of code that hooks into form submission and sends data offsite is a clear violation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or fraud detection scripts may monitor form submissions, but they do not exfiltrate raw payment data to unknown domains.
key_indicators: Appended code to a third-party library
Outbound network request to untrusted domain
Use of obfuscation or encoding (e.g., btoa)
No user interaction or consent for data exfiltration

attack_chain.action: Attacker exploits unpatched Magento to gain access to the web server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to modify static assets served to users.

attack_chain.action: Attacker appends malicious JavaScript to the end of the modernizr.js library.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is served to all users loading the payment page.

attack_chain.action: When a user loads the payment page, the malicious code executes in their browser.
attack_chain.leads_to: Code hooks into the payment form and waits for submission.

attack_chain.action: On form submission, the code collects payment details and exfiltrates them to the attacker's server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen credit card data.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected JavaScript code appended to trusted libraries
JavaScript accessing payment form fields and sending data to external domains
Outbound network requests triggered on form submission to non-whitelisted domains
file_indicators: modernizr.js with appended or modified code not matching official release
Presence of unfamiliar script tags or inline event listeners in payment pages
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP(S) requests to domains not associated with the organization (e.g., malicious-domain.com)
Unusual image or beacon requests during payment form submission
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor static assets for unauthorized changes by comparing deployed files to known-good hashes. Use Content Security Policy (CSP) to restrict outbound requests from payment pages. Inspect JavaScript for unexpected event listeners or data exfiltration logic. Monitor network traffic for requests to untrusted domains, especially during sensitive operations like payment submissions.
